messages.author: 1167fabdc1ff491d
messages.subject: Filtering by loci and individuals
parts:
Hello everybody!

I have a matrix of 71585 loci and 94 individuals divided into 6 populations. I need to filter my matrix but I am wondering if  there is some function that enable me do it in a way that the loci filtered are present in at least 50% of the individuals in each population.

Also, I am trying to understand the mathematics of the missing data. In my whole data (71585 loci), when I use the comand gl.report.callrate, it shows me that 1483 loci do not have missing data. Does it mean that those loci are present in all the 94 individuals? I am asking this because when I use the same comand for one of my populations, it shows that the population only have 996 loci and 330 among them have missing data. I am really confused.

I appreciate the support!
Kind regards,

Jessika

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: Filtering by loci and individuals
parts:
Hi Jessika,

You should use gl.report.callrate(gl, method="ind", plot=TRUE) to examine the call rate across individuals, then choose a threshold value to use in gl.filter.callrate(gl, method="ind", threshold=##). To answer your question, there is no quick way to select loci that are present in 50% of individuals apart from looking at the plot and tablulation by individual, and picking a suitable threshold.

Missing data is typically not "missing" in the sense that it was missed because of poor sequencing coverage, but "missing" because of a mutation at one or both of the restriction enzyme sites leading to fragment dropout. Missing data in the DArT dataset is more like null alleles.

So in your case, you have 71,585 loci of which 1,483 have been successfully scored across all individuals in your dataset. So you have it right.

Why then only 330 of 996 loci for one of your populations? I agree that is confusing. The most likely cause of this apparent discrepancy is that selecting only one population generates a number of monomorphic loci which are then removed (you can switch this off), and some of these would have been among the 1,483 with 100% call rate in the full dataset. So presumably, 1,153 of the 1,483 loci were monomorphic in the single population you are now considering. I would have to have a look at your data to confirm exactly what is going on.

I hope this helps. Please note the updated gl.report.callrate posted in response to a query earlier.

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: Filtering by loci and individuals
parts:
Hi Jessika,

Just following up on this. Your population assignments look fine, so no problem there. You can switch off filtering out monomorphs by setting the parameter mono.rm = FALSE when you run gl.filter.callrate.

Hope this helps.
